title: Refraining From Unilateral Decisions Applies to Everyone on the Team, Not Just Leaders
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece extends the familiar idea that good leaders don't make unilateral decisions affecting their teams into a reciprocal obligation: team members owe leaders the same courtesy. The author explains why inclusive decision-making builds loyalty and commitment when leaders practice it, then pivots to argue that the same standard should apply in reverse, particularly around decisions like leaving the organization. The essay acknowledges this expectation is often treated as unrealistic in practice, but insists there's a meaningful difference between an aspiration and an enforceable rule, and that naming the expectation openly changes behavior on both sides. It ultimately frames inclusive culture as a two-way contract rather than a leader-only discipline.
points: The essay's central reframe is that inclusive decision-making is a mutual obligation, not a one-directional leadership virtue.
It specifically calls out withholding early notice of intent to leave as a violation of the same principle team members expect from leaders.
The piece distinguishes between an expectation and a mandate, arguing that naming the standard explicitly (even without enforcement power) shapes behavior.
It ties the practice directly to loyalty and retention outcomes, not just to abstract fairness.
quotes: Wise leaders do their best to make and keep the promise that they will not make unilateral decisions that affect others without first seeking their input.
Team members are more likely to stay put when they follow a leader who refrains from making unilateral decisions.
If they are “thinking” of leaving the team, the leader would like to learn about it before a final decision is made.
Leaders who refrain from making unliteral decisions that affect team members have every right to ask for reciprocity.
When leaders AND team members refrain from unilateral decision-making, a higher and more reciprocal trust is shared by everyone on the team.
